headline: High-risk shared-filesystem pair: default write access and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write the same filesystem, and Goose also uses MCP while Open Interpreter can ingest clipboard/files and execute code. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge even without a documented direct channel. The pathway is not provably blocked, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF either agent consumes files produced by the other as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared workspace is used for both agents
IF MCP or clipboard content is treated as trusted
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff
Require provenance tags on inter-agent files
Review any MCP server inputs before execution
Use manual copy/paste only for short, human-reviewed snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files and have broad network egress, so sensitive source code or cwd contents can flow out through either agent’s model-provider calls or extensions. Goose explicitly handles model-provider keys and extension tokens; Open Interpreter handles model provider API keys. The shared filesystem makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent sends file contents to a remote model provider
IF secrets are stored in cwd or adjacent config files
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or directories
Disable remote model providers for sensitive tasks
Redact files before handing them to either agent
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification, and both share state via the filesystem. Without locking, concurrent edits can clobber files or corrupt git history. This is a default dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same checkout or working directory
IF either agent modifies git state while the other is active
IF no external file-locking or task partitioning is enforced
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for separation
Add a file-locking wrapper around write operations
Review and reconcile diffs before any commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can emit tool-driven outputs from MCP-enabled workflows, and Open Interpreter can act on code blocks and filesystem state. If Open Interpreter treats Goose’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into executed shell commands or file changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Goose output without independent verification
IF Goose-generated instructions are copied into Open Interpreter tasks
IF either agent is allowed to execute actions from the other’s text verbatim
mitigations: Require human verification before execution
Force Open Interpreter to re-derive critical steps
Keep Goose outputs as suggestions only
Block direct handoff of executable commands
Use a checklist for any action-taking step

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but their default data handling differs: Goose touches source code and cwd files, while Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem at user privilege. That mismatch can create retention and residency issues for regulated data stored locally, even though no specific HIPAA/GDPR claim is documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data resides anywhere on the local machine
IF either agent processes data subject to retention or residency rules
IF the workspace contains data with stricter handling requirements than source code
mitigations: Exclude regulated folders from both agents
Use a dedicated non-regulated workspace
Document retention expectations before use
Delete transient artifacts after each session
Run compliance-sensitive tasks in a separate environment
